claim: Grieser and Maronna prove that area, perimeter, and the sum of the reciprocals of the three angles determine a Euclidean triangle uniquely, giving a new proof that one can hear the shape of a triangle.
stance_target: whether finite-invariant recovery results in inverse spectral triangle geometry are determinacy statements or stability statements
quoted_support: The central point of the argument is to show that area, perimeter and the sum of the reciprocals of the angles determine a triangle uniquely. This is proved using convexity arguments and the partial fraction expansion of $\sin^{-2}x$.

claim: The Grieser-Maronna result is a pure exact-recovery/determinacy theorem with no perturbation, error bound, or modulus-of-continuity analysis anywhere in the stated abstract.
stance_target: quantitative stability is largely absent as a genre in finite-invariant inverse spectral triangle/polygon geometry
scope_conditions: as stated in the arXiv abstract page, math.SP 35P99, 35R30, 51N20
quoted_support: In 1966 Mark Kac asked the famous question 'Can one hear the shape of a drum?'. While this was later shown to be false in general, it was proved by C. Durso that one can hear the shape of a triangle.

claim: The published version of Grieser-Maronna's paper is Notices of the AMS 60(11):1440-1447 (2013), DOI 10.1090/noti1063, which resolves (verified via HTTP redirect) to the AMS journal item page pii=noti1063.
stance_target: bibliographic record for a competing/adjacent finite-invariant determinacy result
